# S43 — verify's git cross-check emits permanent, unclearable warnings

**Findings:** dogfooding; felt every run · **Size: S** · **Tree:** slicer

## Why

`verify.against_git` warns "recorded done, but no commit subject mentions it" for items
finished in a prior repository, and "recorded open, but a commit mentions it" for
maintenance commits that name an id in their subject. Four of these fire on this very
repo every run, and none can be cleared — the history that would satisfy them does not
exist and never will. A check whose warnings can never go green is one people learn to
ignore, which erodes the real signal.

## Files

- `src/slicer/verify.py` — `against_git`
- `src/slicer/config.py` — a toggle, if that is the chosen mechanism

## Failing tests

1. The git cross-check can be disabled by config and then emits nothing.
2. A maintenance commit naming an id in a non-completing way does not flag an open item,
   or there is a way to acknowledge it.

## Implement

Give the git cross-check an off switch in config, and consider narrowing it so a commit
subject that merely references an id (a roadmap-maintenance commit) does not read as
"this open item was secretly finished". The aim is that a clean project reports nothing,
so a warning always means something.

**Not in this slice:** recording per-item content history (S20), which is the deeper fix
for "did this actually land".

## Check

A healthy project's `verify` is quiet; a warning means a real discrepancy.

## Git

One commit.
